chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Abi Nasr from Dawud ibn Sirhan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I accept the testimony of women regarding a child, whether it cried or did not cry, and in everything that a man does not look at, the testimony of women is accepted regarding it.

key_terms.لاَ يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهِ الرَّجُلُ: That which a man does not look at

ai.seo_question: When is the testimony of women accepted in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the scope of female testimony, validating it for matters of child care and private domains where male observation is limited. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that women’s testimony is not inherently inferior but context-dependent, particularly in domestic and biological spheres. It underscores the practical application of *shahadah* in family law, ensuring justice in areas traditionally managed by women.
